finding: Nsight Compute: the 2D kernels (v0-v2) were limited by L1/shared-memory throughput, not DRAM bandwidth, so cutting global loads gave much less speed-up than expected.
The separable kernel does 2(2r+1) instead of (2r+1)^2 multiply-adds per pixel and becomes partly DRAM-bound.
Above 15 taps, NPP falls off a cliff: up to 9.9x slower than the separable kernel.
The separable result is more accurate than the 2D one. FP16 and 8-bit storage variants were also measured.
A sudden 7x slowdown with no code change was traced with nvidia-smi to the laptop GPU's power state.
All kernels ran clean under Compute Sanitizer memcheck (with leak check), racecheck, initcheck and synccheck, including 1000x777 images and the maximum 64x64 shared tile.
